headline: Highest risk is medium: plano can ingest and transmit content while godot_rl_agents is local-only, creating limited prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel or IO surfaces, so direct injection into godot_rl_agents is not documented. B can call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and handle files, so if operators manually bridge A’s outputs into B, prompt-like content could influence B. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual setup.
conditions: IF operators manually copy A outputs into B prompts or config files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace is introduced between the agents, B may parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste of model outputs into B prompts.
Add a review step before B consumes any text from A.
Use provenance labels on all transferred artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B touches logs/metrics/traces and has broad egress plus an API-calling surface. If A’s outputs or artifacts are placed into B’s context, B can transmit them to a third party by default. The pairwise leakage path is indirect but real.
conditions: IF A outputs are copied into B context, those contents may leave the local environment via B egress.
IF B is configured with sensitive logs or traces, those data classes can be transmitted externally.
mitigations: Do not feed sensitive A artifacts into B.
Restrict B egress to approved endpoints only.
Redact logs/traces before B processes them.
Separate storage for A outputs and B inputs.
requires-engineering: add DLP/provenance filtering on B egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or concurrency surfaces documented, while B has broad network egress but no subprocesses and no multiple-instance support. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so conflict is limited to unusual orchestration mistakes rather than default contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable config or API credentials, write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator shares a single state file between them, last-writer-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate credentials to each agent.
Use separate config files for A and B.
Avoid shared mutable state.
Serialize any updates through one operator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a game-playing agent with no documented verification or downstream action controls, and B is a travel-planning agent that can call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If A’s outputs are forwarded into B, B may treat them as authoritative without a built-in verification step. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF A outputs are used as B inputs without human review, B may propagate errors.
IF B is tasked to act on A-generated facts, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between A and B.
Require citations or source links before B acts.
Limit B to drafting, not executing, actions.
Compare A outputs against an independent source.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, or certification claims are documented for either agent. A touches no data classes and B only lists logs/metrics/traces, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess. The other agent is not cited beyond confirming the absence of relevant regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, a separate compliance review is required.
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review residency and retention settings if data classes change.
